intro: Memory is not one thing. Production agents juggle five distinct stores with different write rules, retrieval mechanisms, and retention horizons. Confusing them is the root of most context-bloat bugs.

items.title: Scratchpad
items.whenToUse: Within-turn working notes the model writes to itself between tool calls.
items.mechanism: Lives in the current message list. Created by thinking blocks or assistant text. Discarded when the turn closes (or kept if the loop continues).
items.tradeoff: Free, automatic, ephemeral. Easy to blow the context window if not compacted.

items.title: Working memory (conversation buffer)
items.whenToUse: Across-turn but same-session context: recent messages, tool results, current sub-goal.
items.mechanism: The full message list passed each turn. Often sliding-windowed or summarized when it grows past a budget.
items.tradeoff: Direct, no retrieval overhead. Token cost grows linearly with conversation length unless compacted.

items.title: Episodic memory
items.whenToUse: Specific past interactions — 'remember when we discussed X two weeks ago'.
items.mechanism: External store (vector + metadata). On each turn, retrieve top-K similar prior episodes and inject as labeled context.
items.tradeoff: Scales to arbitrary history. Adds retrieval latency + a category of relevance bugs. Privacy footprint.

items.title: Semantic memory
items.whenToUse: Distilled facts the agent knows about the user, world, or task ('the user prefers SI units', 'API X returns ISO-8601 dates').
items.mechanism: Updated by a slower offline (or end-of-session) summarizer. Read at the start of every conversation.
items.tradeoff: Tiny, persistent, durable. Risk of stale or contradictory facts — needs a write-with-evidence policy.

items.title: Procedural memory
items.whenToUse: Skills / playbooks the agent has accumulated ('to deploy, run X then Y then Z').
items.mechanism: Versioned markdown or code files retrieved by skill name. Anthropic Skills + CLAUDE.md files are exactly this.
items.tradeoff: Most powerful and least flashy of the five. Pays compounding interest as the corpus grows.

pitfalls.title: Unbounded scratchpad
pitfalls.body: Agent writes long internal monologues every step. After 20 steps the prompt is 80% old monologue and 20% current state. Truncate or summarize aggressively.

pitfalls.title: Episodic dump = context bloat
pitfalls.body: Retrieving top-20 past episodes each turn floods working memory. Cap K low, prefer summaries over raw transcripts, dedupe before injecting.

pitfalls.title: No compaction strategy
pitfalls.body: Turn 30 is paying token cost for turn 1's tool results. Pick a compaction trigger (turn count, token budget, idle minutes) and a strategy (summarize, drop, archive).

pitfalls.title: Semantic memory drift
pitfalls.body: Agent updates 'user prefers Spanish' on a one-off Spanish message. Require evidence count or confidence before writing a long-lived fact.

pitfalls.title: Treating procedures as tools
pitfalls.body: A playbook called as a tool returns a giant blob into context. Better: load procedural memory once at session start, not on every step.
